description: Which identity runs each appliance service, who may read keys and state, and which local sockets carry Party <-> game traffic. avrana/ops/boundary.py evaluates a host against it; nothing here is applied to a host by this repository.

front.name: avrana-front
front.means: may connect to a native game's socket

games.name: avrana-games
games.means: may connect to Party Core's internal socket; a supplementary group of every native-game unit

keys.delivery: Party Core reads its own store; every other holder receives exactly its own keys through LoadCredential

phases.1: before the field test: the three existing services leave the operator account; Party-owned key store, credentials for every other holder, read-only code, owned state, loopback-only TCP
phases.2: native games: a dynamic identity each, one group-gated Unix socket each, Party Core's internal socket, no IP networking
phases.3: the legacy shared LAN Games process is gone
